facts.text: Tompkinsville was founded in 1815 by New York Governor Daniel D. Tompkins, the state's fourth governor.
The neighborhood sits on Staten Island’s eastern shore, overlooking Upper New York Bay, and is part of the North Shore.
In 1817 Tompkins built a dock at the foot of present‑day Victory Boulevard and began offering steam ferry service to Manhattan.
The historic waterfront once hosted shipyards, ferry docks, and warehouses, while inland rowhouses and churches echo late‑19th‑century prosperity.
The area’s name honors Governor Tompkins, and the early telephone exchange that served the eastern North Shore was also called Tompkinsville before becoming Saint George.
Community groups have recently cleaned up Tappen Park and Bay Street, and preservationists protect surviving 19th‑century homes and civic structures.
